caveats: The model plays practice boards only while a stage quest holds him (balance.json model.practice): its days per 回 run long.

The model plays no 杂役 errands and no 开府: 灵石 earned is low, affordability pessimistic. It takes a share of the day's wall tags (balance.json `walls`), the rest while a gate holds him (a gate's wait counts them).
A 回 holds him on its stage quest's layer (else its cap); a 今 interlude takes the 古 before it.
A day of sitting = one night of 闭关 (rewards.json seclusion rest_hours) at the layer, as the rules pay it.

checked.text: A qi-gathering pill from the garden's culls, nine gold rings on it. In the first layers of Qi Condensation the market's is worth a few hours' sitting; this, three days. Higher up, both are worth less.

wm-mingpai/over.why: Hanli's own call (2026-11-09, kept 2026-11-10): the first night in the 石室, which the book tells as the gain (wm-kaikai: 「第一天夜里，二层圆满，跟着第三层的关口在他身子里「咯」地一响」) — the 秘境's buried-earth night he named as the one exception to 「不要白给修为, 除了像秘境埋土里那次, 剧情里明确写了突破的」. Kept as written; a story step there would pay one small game's (the report shows both).

mend-pill-9.why: The book (its card): 「骨伤也治得好，修为也跟着涨一截」 — the 九转回春丹 mends and lifts cultivation a little: two nights of 闭关 at its level (40 修为 at 练气一层; 九转聚气丹's 3, 「涨一截」 the smaller) beside its full heal; until 2026-11-10 it paid 3 nights and healed nothing. One night (20) moved the typical 古七 7.0 → 6.6 days and 古八 12.5 → 12.6 (it is eaten in 古四, wm-diyilu): two keep the pace as it was (tools/balance.mjs).

games.games.haggle.stage.why: The 游戏厅's 砍价 stage (games.json haggle `stage`) sets up a practice save that walks in with 300 灵石 to haggle with — a wallet he holds, never a grant paid; the arcade's fixture, not the economy.

chapters.00-prologue.scenes.00-waimen.ex.why: The book tells the toll: 外门's 公中 takes 「一块灵石」 (00-waimen: 「收了你一块灵石」 · 「一块灵石，买一个「懂事」」) — a price the story states, asked and taken as written.

chapters.00-waimen.scenes.wm-mijing.exit.why: The book tells the toll: 马小宝's 公中 takes 「两块」 at the 秘境's door (wm-mijing, its refusal 「怀里的灵石，不够两块」) — a price the story states, asked and taken as written.

chapters.00-prologue.scenes.00-hall.exit.why: The book tells the allowance: three stones at the 入门 (00-waimen: 「他把怀里的灵石一块一块放进他娘给的那个空钱袋里，叮，叮，叮」), one of them the 公中's next morning — paid as written.
